# Weavers of the Void®: The Rules of the World

Every world runs on a book of rules: how fast peoples grow, how often wars break out, how long a curse lingers, how far a god's hand can reach. This booklet lists every one of them with the value a new world starts from and the range it may take. You can change any of them for your own world from World rules in the settings.

## How to read this booklet

- The rules are gathered into **chapters** and, within each chapter, into **topics**, in the same order as World rules in the settings.
- **Starts at** is the value every new world begins with.
- **Range** runs from the lowest value the rule accepts to the highest value advised. You may go above the advised highest value; the game warns you but lets the world run. You may not go below the lowest.
- An epoch lasts 50 years unless your world says otherwise. Rules counted in years follow your world's epoch length.
- **Tied to** names the mechanics of the world that this rule governs directly. The companion booklet *How the World Connects* describes each of them.
- A rule marked **in order** belongs to a set whose values must rise from one to the next; the last chapter lists those sets.

### Engine phases

#### Engine budget

| Rule | Starts at | Range | Tied to |
|---|---:|---|---|
| <a id="r-engine_budget-max_sub_steps_per_epoch"></a>Most campaign seasons and sampled years the engine evaluates in one epoch | 400 | 1 to 1,000,000 | — |
| <a id="r-engine_budget-tick_target_seconds"></a>Seconds one engine tick of the reference world should stay under | 20 | 1 to 3,600 | — |
| <a id="r-engine_budget-workers"></a>Worker processes that compute the shards of an engine step in parallel; 0 uses one fewer than the cores | 0 | 0 to 256 | — |
| <a id="r-engine_budget-regression_pct"></a>Growth of the work of a tick of the reference world beyond its budget that fails the benchmark (%) | 15% | 0% to 1,000% | — |
| <a id="r-engine_budget-prehistory_seconds_per_epoch"></a>Seconds one round of a prehistory should stay under; a slower round is reported in the prehistory's record | 10 | 1 to 3,600 | — |

Pilotage: pilots who know the shoals bring ships in and out of harbour; Positional reckoning: numbers are written by place and reckoned with a zero; Postal service: couriers carry letters along set roads; Railways: engines haul loads along iron rails; Refrigeration: machines keep food cold; Rocketry: rockets carry craft between worlds without magic; Ropemaking: fibres are laid and twisted into rope and cord; Shipwrighting: hulls for open seas and war; Siegecraft: sappers and engines take walls; Sky sailing: ships sail the air between worlds; Skysteel: star-fallen metal is worked; Standing army administration: soldiers are paid and kept; Star forts: low angled walls turn cannon shot; Star navigation: ships steer by the stars; Steam power: boiling water drives engines; Steamships: ships sail against wind and current under steam; Steel: iron is hardened into steel; Summoning: beings are called from elsewhere; Surgery: healers cut out what festers; Telegraph: messages run along wires in an instant; Telephone: voices are carried along wires; Terracing: hills are cut into fields; The fortress: castles command the land; The plough: beasts turn the soil; Universities: scholars gather to teach; Vaccines: a mild exposure guards against a deadly sickness; Volley drill: ranks load and fire by command; #### Star life

| Rule | Starts at | Range | Tied to |
|---|---:|---|---|
| <a id="r-star_life-old_dimming"></a>Brightness an old star loses each epoch | 1 | 0 to 50 | — |
